articles.title: GTA 6: Everything the New Screenshots Tell Us
articles.summary: The latest GTA 6 screenshots showcase a bunch of great new features, from tropical storms and hunting, to simulated citrus farms and beach-ready butts.
articles.body:
A huge amount of new GTA 6 information has arrived in the world courtesy of the latest issue of Game Informer. The magazine’s new cover story has revealed over 20 major new details , including how the world simulates tropical storms and some of the many animals that call Leonida home.

Arriving alongside all this new information is 12 brand new screenshots, provided by Rockstar for Game Informer’s exclusive coverage . That exclusivity means we can’t post them here on IGN, but we would like to talk about them, because many of them tell a deeper story about Grand Theft Auto 6. Across the dozen images, we can see many of the newly-revealed features in action, and the scenarios depicted point to gameplay functions that may well be present in the full game.

These new screenshots reintroduce us to the First Chapter, a Leonida motorcycle gang. Game Informer’s cover story explains that the Ambrosia region of the map is home to a “local biker gang calling the shots”, and it very much looks like we’ll be butting heads with them – we can see Jason making a hasty getaway from a few armed gang members.

The First Chapter likely operates all over Ambrosia, but it seems like The Thirsty Wolf is one of their local hang outs. These screenshots show the bar’s wooden interior, as well as what may well be its interior. Rockstar Games’ head of development/co-studio head, Aaron Garbut, told Game Informer that “the buildings are more real inside and out”, and this bar certainly has every authentic detail you’d expect, from the beer to the pool table to the neon lights promoting its titillating entertainment.

We’ve seen the First Chapter’s uniform before, which includes a badge that seems to denote the biker’s rank – in these latest screenshots, the most prominent biker is a Sergeant-at-Arms. This marks him as the club’s primary enforcer, and so there’s a good chance it’s this guy that Jason has pissed off.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Look closely at the Sergeant-at-Arms and you’ll find a couple of very cool details. The first is, of course, his tattoos, which are classic biker designs. Rockstar’s vice president of dynamic art, Michael Kane, told Game Informer that the team “paid a crazy amount of attention” to ensuring the tattoos of each of the world’s communities felt culturally correct. And since we know we can go to a tattoo parlor to get ink of our own, it’s likely that at least some of the designs we’ve seen can be applied to Jason and Lucia’s skin.

But we’ve had tattoos in GTA before. What we’ve not seen before is sunburn. The Sergeant’s face is burned pink from being out in the sun, but the space around his eyes remains untouched thanks to his sunglasses. I wouldn’t take this as a sign that you need to regularly apply SPF in-game, but it certainly shows the wild level of detail Rockstar’s artists are applying to each character. The woman standing behind him has a freckled face, and the studio has confirmed that skin features like tanning and moles will also be represented.

We already know that GTA 6 is set to feature the widest array of body types the series has ever had, and a new screenshot taken on Vice City’s beach showcases this perfectly. Both Jason and Lucia are notably toned, likely as a result of heading to the gym, which can improve muscle definition. But Rockstar revealed to Game Informer that characters will have localised weight gain, meaning they can carry fat on their chest, stomach, and even butts.

That would explain why there’s someone on the beach taking a photo of their friend’s arse. There’s a cake for every kind of person, apparently, so why not stick it on social media?

Talking of social media, that same beach screenshot shows both a sunbathing woman and Jason scrolling on their phone. We’ve known since GTA 6’s very first TikTok-filled trailer that online communities would be part of the world, and Game Informer has confirmed that Snapmatic is back, which will presumably present a feed filled with cheeks. Just remember, you can only scroll, not post yourself – as criminals, Jason and Lucia are looking to maintain a low profile.

Just because we can’t post doesn’t mean we can’t take photos, though, and aside from the bizarre beach photo shoot, these new screenshots also show a man using an SLR-style camera in Mount Kalaga National Park. Previous GTA games have let us use a camera for both reconnaissance and photography, so that may make a return here.

That same screenshot shows Jason and Lucia going for a run through the park, suggesting a couples 5k could be on the cards for casual dates. They’re both dressed in athleisure wear – is this just a case of a well-costumed screenshot, or is there perhaps a wardrobe system for pre-preparing appropriate outfits for different activities?

Regardless of if you have to manually go to a wardrobe to dress or if there’s an automatic system, the world’s clothing has been painstakingly created to reflect Florida’s local culture and fashion trends. “We’ve been able to really go hard on that with creating the biggest range of garments and accessories we’ve ever made – supported with rich, realistic materials,” Kane told Game Informer.

Across GTA 6’s many trailers, we’ve already seen a plethora of different activities we’ll be able to participate in, including base jumping, air boating, kayaking, and the gym. Game Informer’s article also confirms mini golf, scuba diving, going to the zoo, and billiards — the latter of which can be seen in the biker bar screenshot. Just don’t let the staff distract you from potting the right ball.

Another activity we’ll be able to take part in is hunting. Rockstar had already confirmed that fishing is possible, although we don’t know the full extent of the system yet. The latest screenshot of the Everglades-like Grassrivers region features a wooden cage for catching crabs and lobsters – is this just set dressing, or an indication that the fishing could be deeper than just casting a line?

The two fellas in that same screenshot are holding out against some incoming alligators, which is a pretty unconventional way of hunting. Hunting is a side activity in GTA 6, though, and we can see what looks like a more conventional version of it in the screenshot featuring Jason, a rifle, and a couple of deer. This type of game hunting is lifted from Red Dead Redemption 2, but it will likely have been modernised for GTA’s 21st century setting. For example, Jason’s wearing olive green attire – perhaps wearing colours that help you blend into your environment will keep you concealed from your prey?

Jason’s rifle has also been kitted out with an autumnal woodland camo pattern. Previous screenshots have showcased weapon skins and modifications, but these latest images continue to demonstrate the breadth of what’s available. Similarly, a new screenshot shows Lucia holding an M4 assault rifle fitted with a silencer, red-dot scope, and forward grip – it seems like the weapon modification options will rival those seen in big first-person shooters.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

While that M4 will come in handy when hunting humans, the big game stalking side activity will naturally target animals. Game Informer’s article reveals that the creatures you’ll be assigned to track will be divided into three categories: rare, discoverable, and legendary. Presumably these will be special breeds, rather than the generic species you can find all over the world.

Rockstar revealed to Game Informer that there are 170 species of animal , including over 60 birds and 30 land mammals. We see a number of them across the new screenshots, including domestic dogs, alligators, buck and doe deers, ducks, and seagulls. In the screenshot of Jason fleeing The Thirsty Wolf, we can even see two pigeons picking through trash, an indicator that each animal species may display recognisable real-world behaviour.

Perhaps the biggest reveal of the Game Informer article is the news that GTA 6 will feature incredibly detailed dynamic weather . Owen Shepherd, Rockstar’s vice president of art for lighting and rendering, explained that there will be fully dynamic cloudscapes, allowing for a broad spectrum of weather conditions. Regions will have localised rain showers, and Florida’s famous stormy skies will be replicated. We can see such an event happening in one of the screenshots, which shows a plane flying towards thick grey clouds peppered with lightning strikes.

Rockstar hasn’t just focused on the big, dramatic weather, though. Rain will leave a layer of water across surfaces that remains after the storm passes. The puddles we can see on the floor in the screenshot of The Thirsty Wolf were likely left by one of those dynamic rain showers.

One of Game Informer’s least exciting new screenshots shows a plane flying over a set of trees. But while that may be a little dull on the surface, dig into the details and you can really see the developer’s ambition on show.

To begin with, this image shows an orange grove – the parked pickup reveals it’s called Tucker’s Citrus Farms. Along the line of orange trees we can see workers using tools to harvest the oranges and pack them into crates.

There was surely absolutely no need for Rockstar to have created a simulated citrus farm (although if Jason and Lucia embark on a marmalade raid, I’ll eat my words). But the studio has done so in pursuit of creating an authentic representation of its inspiration state. Tucker’s is located on the Leonida-Gloriana line, GTA’s version of the Florida-Georgia line, and will likely play a part in creating an appropriate atmosphere for this more “country” area of Leonida. It’s clear Rockstar values that authentic world as much as any gameplay feature.

There’s more detail in this screenshot, though: the overhead plane has kicked up a dust storm. We can see a worker coughing, and another having dropped to their hands and knees to avoid breathing in the particles. This suggests a wild level of simulation, one where passing aircraft can disrupt vegetation to create particle clouds that cause NPCs to react in ways that make it appear that a bunch of polygons has a respiratory system. Maybe that’s an illusion painted by a nicely arranged screenshot, but considering so many of these images seem designed to showcase features that Rockstar have discussed, I wouldn’t be surprised if the simulation really is this deep.

We’ve still got much to learn, and it won’t be until we play GTA 6 ourselves that we’ll know if everything these screenshots suggest are reality. But until then, what did you spot in these new screenshots? And what newly-revealed features are you most excited for? Let us know in the comments.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Scrubs Returns for Season 11, and the Beloved Medical Sitcom Is Funnier and More Heartwarming Than Ever
articles.summary: Scrubs Season 11 is off to a strong start, as this charming sitcom looks to improve on some of the flaws of Season 10. Read our review of the first two episodes.
articles.body:
The first two episodes of Scrubs Season 11 premiere on ABC on September 30 and on Hulu on October 1.

In an era where it's become customary to wait years between new seasons of many popular shows, it's certainly a treat to receive two seasons of Scrubs in the same calendar year. The previous revival season proved to be the ultimate sitcom comfort food. It effortlessly wiped away the stigma of Season 9 and won fans back over with its depiction of the eternal bromance between Drs. John Dorian (Zach Braff) and Christopher Turk (Donald Faison). Season 10 wasn't without its problems, but it was a fun little romp that recaptured the charming vibe of the original series. Season 11 is much the same, but with a slightly more ambitious storytelling approach added for good measure.

Naturally, Braff and Faison remain in the spotlight for Season 11, as does Sarah Chalke's Dr. Elliot Reid. Much of the new cast introduced in Season 10 also returns, with Ava Bunn's Sam Tosh now upped to series regular. Unfortunately, Season 11 eliminates two of the more memorable supporting cast members in Joel Kim Booster's Dr. Kevin Park and X Mayo's Nurse Pippa Raymond. It's not the worst thing in the world for the series to trim its ensemble cast a bit, but neither character deserved to be on the chopping block.

Season 10 did suffer at times from the lack of focus on classic Scrubs characters like Dr. Cox (John C. McGinley) and Nurse Carla Espinosa (Judy Reyes). Thankfully, that changed late in the game as the now-retired Dr. Cox came roaring back into Sacred Heart and grappled with his own mortality. One of the perks of Season 11 is that it continues that storyline rather than simply moving on. In fact, there are hints of a more serialized narrative this season. The show really leans into Cox's ongoing health struggles and J.D.'s desperate attempts to care for his prickly mentor. Mind you, Scrubs is in no danger of turning into The Pitt anytime soon, but it is nice to get a bit more drama and see a little more connective tissue between these first two episodes. And if that approach keeps McGinley's hilarious character in the picture longer this season, so much the better.

If Scrubs is being a bit more ambitious with its storytelling this season, it certainly never loses sight of the fact that fans are here first and foremost for the dynamic between J.D., Turk, and Elliot. All three characters get ample room to shine in these first two episodes. J.D and Turk have several memorable bonding scenes together, and the series is ever on-point with J.D.'s fanciful dream sequences. There's one cutaway that rivals Season 10's detective noir scene for its sheer zaniness. And with Elliot, the series continues finding ways to explore and enrich the character outside the shackles of the "Will they, won't they?" format the original series was so fixated on.

But what of the newbies? As enjoyable as it was, Season 10 never fully cemented its new cast of interns. There were simply too many of these characters, and they never felt like a priority for the series amid the emphasis on the core doctor trinity. These two episodes show signs that the writers are looking to narrow their focus a bit this time. Obviously, Bunn's Tosh is a bigger priority now, and Episode 2 makes some inroads in terms of defining her as more than "the social media-obsessed one."

In fact, Episode 2, which is titled "My Mentee," seems to cement a new status quo where each of the three leads is paired with a different underling, mirroring the Cox/J.D. dynamic of the original show. Elliott gets Tosh, Turk gets Dr. Dashana Trainor (Amanda Morrow), and J.D. struggles to connect with the new chief resident, Dr. Grant Summers (John Higgins). This narrowed focus is promising, though it does serve to make the rest of the interns like Asher (Jacob Dudman) and Blake (David Gridley) feel even more superfluous than before. We'll see if Season 11 can ultimately achieve a better balance than its predecessor, but things are looking promising so far.

articles.title: ‘Xbox is not for sale’ says Microsoft’s gaming chief
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is taking a ‘long-term view’ of Microsoft’s gaming division.
articles.body: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports that Microsoft is considering selling off its Xbox business. The Information reported in June that Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood had been considering spinning out Xbox entirely, and then reported earlier this month that both execs have “more recently supported Sharma’s plans to overhaul the unit.” “Xbox is not for sale,” says Sharma in an interview with The New York Times. “We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model and everything needed to achieve that.” It appears that Nadella and Hood have favored the giant Xbox “reset” as the plan for Microsoft’s gaming unit instead of making Xbox a joint venture or spinning out the gaming business entirely. Sharma announced her Xbox restructuring in June, calling it a reset for the division. Microsoft is planning to lay off up to 3,200 Xbox employees over the course of its 2027 financial year, which ends in June. Nadella backed Sharma’s restructuring and layoffs in a recent appearance on the Sources podcast. “There’s some amount of streamlining the team is doing, and Asha is doing, which is great to see,” said Nadella last week. “And then we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.” The most recent restructuring has seen Halo move under Activision, as well as the developers behind Sea of Thieves and Age of Empires. Alongside a major shake-up of Xbox Game Studios, the recent changes look geared toward making Xbox a wholly owned subsidiary like Microsoft does with LinkedIn. Microsoft is reducing management layers at Xbox, offloading smaller studios, and focusing on its larger Xbox franchises. That could eventually end in an Xbox sale at some point in the future, but right now the plan seems to be about bringing growth back to Xbox. “We’ve got a long way to go with Microsoft,” says Sharma, “and we’re going to take the long-term view.” But as Sharma said in February, “The plan’s the plan until it’s not the plan.”

articles.title: Microsoft's Deal for Hideo Kojima's Physint 'Substantially Below What Xbox Would Typically Spend to Develop a Premium Game'
articles.summary: Microsoft’s high-profile deal for Hideo Kojima’s Physint is reportedly “substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game.”
articles.body:
Microsoft’s high-profile deal for Hideo Kojima’s Physint is reportedly “substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game.”

Xbox snapped up Physint after Kojima pitched the game to new CEO Asha Sharma — a pitch Kojima conducted after Sony canceled the previously PlayStation-exclusive project. For more on that, check out IGN’s recent interview with Hideo Kojima himself , where he talks through how he found out Sony had ditched Physint, and his concern about the fate of Kojima Productions.

Since then, there have been a number of online reports about the budget for Physint, with some claiming the deal was around $400 million. Subsequent reports claimed the figure was substantially less. Now, in a New York Times profile of Sharma , it was reported that Xbox may have negotiated a deal for less than you’d expect for what is expected to be a full price, triple-A spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid from the creator of the franchise.

Here’s the relevant blurb from the NYT article:

Xbox’s deal for Physint includes adaptations (Death Stranding is getting exactly that). Kojima told IGN that Microsoft was “not thinking of just funding a game. They're thinking about movies and anime. It's more about the IP. Let's create a new IP. And that's bigger in scale, so to speak. And not many other game publishers or game developers have that kind of vision.”

So, whatever the exact figure, we know Xbox is funding Physint the project, not just the video game. So we might see a Physint live-action movie (will it go up against the Metal Gear Solid movie?!), potentially an anime, and maybe even more.

Video game production budgets have risen dramatically in recent years, especially in the west where development costs have skyrocketed. Triple-A video game sales haven’t risen to match these rising costs, putting pressure on the triple-A video game industry.

In the wake of Physint’s move to Xbox, Bloomberg reported that Sony had concerns around the success of Death Stranding, as well as Physint’s development timeline, budget, and platform strategy. Kojima Productions issued a statement in response, although it failed to directly address Bloomberg’s reporting.

“Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications,” Kojima Productions said. “While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.​”

Physint remains without a release window. It is expected after the launch of OD, Kojima's next video game for Xbox.

articles.title: 'We Have Been Gradually Preparing': Capcom Already Has a Plan for When Its Resident Evil Remakes Catch Up With Newer Games
articles.summary: Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."
articles.body:
Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."

That's according to Jun Takeuchi, a Capcom veteran who has served as excutive producer for the series over the past decade, who has acknowledged the fact that Capcom's hugely popular remakes are slowly running out of classic games to re-release. The publisher has already remade Resident Evil 2, 3 and 4 to great success, with a new version of Code Veronica slated for next year.

It has previously been reported that a Resident Evil 0 remake will follow in 2028, and that a Resident Evil 1 remake has also been considered. Of the mainline Resident Evil games, this would then just leave Resident Evil 5 and 6 as the only titles left to get new versions — both of which would be interesting prospects, for separate reasons.

While Capcom likely has enough remakes to keep their releases going for another decade, there will come a point where the publisher needs to decide whether to remake other titles, or start remaking its remakes all over again. Or... do something else, Takeuchi teased.

"The current Resident Evil series is being developed along two tracks," Takeuchi noted, writing in the just-released Biohazard 30th anniversary special magazine book now available in Japan (thanks, RENews_X , via The Gamer ).

"Someday, the remake series will catch up with the era of the numbered titles, and we are already thinking about what we will do when that happens," he continued. "In fact, we have been gradually preparing for that since around Resident Evil Village. The appearance of names such as Umbrella and Spencer, as well as the return of Raccoon City in Requiem, are also in preparation for a 'crossover'.

"At first, we included these elements with the sense that they were fan service, but users were far more delighted by them than we had imagined, and they even began analysing the thoughts that the development team had privately kept to itself. So, as a series, we decided to respond to users' expectations and pushed this setup further in Village and Requiem."

Takeuchi went on to state that Capcom regarded Resident Evil 7 "as a turning point for the series" as it was in development when its plans to start remaking older games really came to fruition. Does this mean that everything before 7 is set to be remade one day, while 7 and onwards is considered too new?

Resident Evil 5 sold hugely well, with particular interest in the game in the wake of the top-rated Resident Evil 4. (Sadly, 5 was nowhere near as good.) But any new version of the game would see Capcom returning to the controversy over 5's African setting and companion character Sheva. As for Resident Evil 6, which featured a range of protagonists, it just isn't very good. But perhaps Capcom could salvage it in an eventual new version?

What's more interesting here is Capcom's suggestion that is using its remakes to seed ideas it will pick up again in newer titles, when that "crossover" point eventually happens. After all, Resident Evil has now been going for 30 years, which is a long time for anyone to remember plot details without being able to revisit early entries.

For now, though, all of that is a long time off — and there's plenty to look forward to. The promising-looking Resident Evil Veronica is next on the docket, and we've already asked Capcom some of our burning questions...

articles.title: 'Xbox Is Not for Sale' — Asha Sharma Denies Reports That Microsoft Is Considering Selling Its Gaming Business
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports suggesting Microsoft was considering selling its gaming business.
articles.body:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports suggesting Microsoft was considering selling its gaming business.

In an interview with the New York Times , Sharma declared: “Xbox is not for sale.”

“We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model and everything needed to achieve that,” Sharma continued.

One of the big questions emerging from Sharma’s appointment as Xbox CEO earlier this year, and the subsequent layoffs and restructuring that have occurred in recent months, revolves around the long-term future of Microsoft’s gaming business. Will Microsoft sell off Xbox? Are the cuts and restructure laying the groundwork for a sale?

Details on a potential shakeup came from The Information (via Reuters ), which said that Microsoft hadn't ruled out turning the Xbox brand into a wholly-owned subsidiary. It said the move could result in Xbox being operated as a joint venture with other partners or even potentially sold.

Sharma’s Xbox reset has since become clearer. Nearly 2,000 Xbox staff have already been cut, with more to come this financial year. Multiple studios have either exited Xbox or face closure , and various games have been canceled . Xbox is now focused on fewer, bigger video game franchises such as The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and Minecraft, with the likes of Halo moved over to Call of Duty company Activision . Through it all, there are question marks hanging over the viability of Xbox’s confirmed next-gen console, Project Helix.

While some believe this reset and the cuts that have come with it are part of a strategy to make Xbox easier to sell, analysts aren’t convinced. Some have said Xbox would likely have few suitors interested in buying the business outright, considering Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard for an eye-watering $69 billion, Xbox’s huge payroll, extensive studio setup, and hardware business. More likely, analysts have suggested, is that big companies may pick off parts of Xbox as Microsoft continues to look to trim the business.

Every Video Game Franchise Xbox Owns After Acquiring Activision Blizzard

The NYT speculates that an eventual spinoff could create an independent Xbox that would partner with Microsoft while keeping its costs off the company’s balance sheet. But Sharma cast doubt on this as an option, too, saying: “We’ve got a long way to go with Microsoft, and we’re going to take the long-term view.”

Who would even buy Xbox when Xbox itself admits its business is unhealthy? Xbox ended the financial year with a 3% accountability margin (assumed to be profit margin), down year-over-year. Excluding Activision Blizzard King, over the past five years Microsoft spent over $20 billion on ongoing investments in what Sharma called its content, platform, and hardware “subsidy,” but annual revenue declined nearly half a billion during that time.

“We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses,” Sharma said in a blog post announcing the layoffs in July. “We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”

Meanwhile, Microsoft has increased the price of Xbox consoles. Microsoft blamed this on console storage and memory prices, which have increased by more than 2.5x, and it expects another doubling by the fall of 2027. "The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles," Microsoft said when it announced the price rises. "... the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history," Sharma added in the Xbox "Reset" memo.

For now, Sharma’s focus is on growing Xbox, which, she told the NYT, still has 500 million players a month. Microsoft's ambitious target is for Xbox to reach 1 billion people a day — a figure that has been ridiculed online. How will Xbox achieve this? By tapping into markets such as Africa and South Asia via cloud computing, and investing in Minecraft as a Roblox competitor, the NYT reported.

articles.title: Vincent D’Onofrio Defends Laufey Star Deborah Ann Woll From Gooners Upset That the Game's Armor Sets Don't Show More Skin
articles.summary: Emmy-nominated actor Vincent D’Onofrio has somehow found himself at war with a self-proclaimed ‘gooner’ over Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance in God of War Laufey.
articles.body:
Emmy-nominated actor Vincent D’Onofrio has somehow found himself at war with a self-proclaimed ‘gooner’ over Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance in God of War Laufey.

The next game in the God of War series is fast approaching, this time following the adventures of Laufey, Kratos’ second wife and Loki’s mother in Norse mythology.

Given the current state of social media, it’s almost unsurprising that this fact alone has riled up the online rage machine — but it seems the controversy has grown so loud that other A-List actors are taking notice.

More recently, the conversation has shifted from Deborah Ann Woll’s in-game appearance as Laufey to her special armor sets within the upcoming game. As told by a Twitter/X user who goes by the name ‘Geralt of Goonia,' Sony’s Santa Monica Studio “would rather go bankrupt than give you an ounce of female attractiveness,” specifically when it comes to how much skin these armor sets cover.

Unexpectedly, Vincent D’Onofrio — who acted alongside Woll in Netflix and Marvel’s Daredevil series — chimed into the conversation to defend his co-star and proclaim his excitement to play the game alongside his son when it releases this coming February.

“Not that you asked, but… In no way do I agree with you,” he wrote. “Deborah is beautiful and extremely talented. She is as smart as a whip and a complete nerd. Also incredibly kind. How perfect she is! And a good friend. I am a fan of God of War. I, for one, cannot wait to play the new game with my son.”

Despite getting owned by Kingpin himself, Geralt of Goonia continued his tirade, leading to no end of humorous responses and memes from players defending Laufey and agreeing with D’Onofrio’s excitement about playing the game.

Laufey has been at the center of a few discussions between notable folks in the gaming and entertainment space lately; the original creator of God of War, David Jaffe, called the game “stupid” during a recent live stream, and accused its creative director, Ariel Lawrence, of having a “lack of passion” for the title itself. (He later clarified these remarks in a tweet and defended Lawrence from the ensuing harassment campaign that started against her as a result of his comments.)

Prior to that, The Last of Us director Bruce Straley used Laufey as an example of AAA games that failed to “excite” him, though he similarly clarified this statement and apologized for bringing "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention” to the title.

Woll, for her part, hasn’t let the negativity get her down. Speaking with a fan at Florida Supercon in July, she said she’s confident that Laufey is a fantastic game, which has, at least in part, helped her avoid being affected by the backlash from trolls online.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad,” she said.

articles.title: MTG Corn Maze Secret Lair Superdrop Brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth, KPop Demon Hunters, and Marvel Zombies to Magic
articles.summary: Wizards of the Coast trots out a new MTG Secret Lair on a monthly basis at this point, and while crossovers aren't anything new, the new 'super drop' brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth and KPop Demon Hunters to the card game for the first time.
articles.body:
Wizards of the Coast trots out a new MTG Secret Lair on a monthly basis at this point, and while crossovers aren't anything new for the franchise, this new 'super drop' brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth and KPop Demon Hunters to the card game for the first time.

Wizards of the Coast has just announced the Corn Maze Superdrop, clearly in time for Halloween, but instead of going with a darker horror twist like it did with the Junji Ito drop, all of these collections are relatively lighthearted. Of course, for most people, the biggest draw is going to be the KPop Demon Hunters and Labyrinth drops – the latter of which has three collections – along with a Marvel: Zombies collection.

The three Labyrinth drops are the highlight of the Corn Maze Superdrop, though. The Secret Lair x Jim Henson's Labyrinth Fear Me, Love Me drop is entirely focused on Goblin kindred cards, and is headlined by Muxus, Goblin Grandee, a Goblin Staple, posing as Jareth, Goblin King with a beautiful illustration of David Bowie. Of course, there's also a copy of Claim the Firstborn as The Kidnapping of Toby. For some reason, though, this drop also has a copy of Trinisphere, which doesn't really fit into any conceivable goblin deck, but at least it has some cool art of Bowie holding a bunch of orbs .

Of course it wouldn't be a Secret Lair Superdrop without some nigh-unreadable cards, and that's where the Secret Lair x Jim Henson's Labyrinth: Through the Labyrinth comes in. The art on these cards are all gorgeous, though I could totally see some of them being hard to parse from across the table. Still, Wizards decided to print Leveler in this drop, which you can combine with The Beamtown Bullies or Thassa's Oracle to make your pod wish they were dropped in the Labyrinth.

There's also a Kpop Demon Hunters drop, which has some incredible cards with combo potential. This one comes with a copy of Freed From The Real and Underworld Breach, both of which will be notorious in decks that are built around them. There's a reason Breach has been banned in multiple formats, after all.

And Wizards is still trying to work more Marvel content into Magic, this time with a Marvel Zombies drop that's focused on Zombie kindred cards. But, as cool as it would be to have a commander deck helmed by Zombie Thor or Zombie Scarlet witch, none of the cards in this drop are really worth the high price you'd be paying for them, unless you really love Marvel Zombies.

Some of the other drops are seriously cool, too. The Manufactured Grounds by See Machine drop brings some incredible art to the original artifact land cycle from Mirrodin. That drop probably doesn't make a lot of sense from a purely financial perspective, but damn, does it look cool. Then there's the Peace, Love and Treefolk drop, which gives Timber Protector its first meaningful reprint besides the Lord of the Rings commander decks.

I'm probably going to pick up all of the Labyrinth drops, and if you want to grab one (or all) of them too, the Corn Maze Superdrop will be available starting at 9am PT / 12pm ET on October 12. Wizards of the Coast will even toss in a Labyrinth-flavored copy of Maze of Ith on any order over $199.

articles.title: European Commission Calls Out Riot, Activision, Mojang, and More Over In-Game Currency and Transactions
articles.summary: The European Commission is taking action against nine video game companies over their digital currency and pricing of in-game items with the goal of protecting players’ rights.
articles.body:
The European Commission is taking action against nine video game companies over their digital currency and pricing of in-game items with the goal of protecting players’ rights.

Launched on September 29, 2026, these actions are a follow-up to the Consumer Protection Cooperation Network’s Key Principles on in-game virtual currencies, which are a set of guidelines released in March 2025 that “promote transparency and fairness” for in-game currency and transactions.

These Key Principles guidelines were reached after the CPC Network had extensive discussions with game studios and publishers — but despite these talks, it found indications that a “high number of video game companies” hadn’t made any substantive changes to their games as a result of its public guidance, “nor as a result of the extensive talks between the CPC Network and the gaming industry that have taken place over the course of the past years.”

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

The CPC Network name-dropped these companies in a joint statement with the European Commission on September 30, publicly asking that they bring their in-game currency and transaction systems in line with their guidelines. These companies include Activision Blizzard UK, Mojang AB, Riot Games Limited, Supercell Oy, and Ubisoft EMEA SAS.

“Some video games directly exhort children to make purchases, despite an explicit prohibition in EU consumer protection law. Consumers across Europe should be able to play and interact with video games without being tricked into spending more money or time on video games than they want,” the CPC Network’s joint statement reads.

As outlined by the European Commission, its newest actions focus on seven core principles: providing clear and transparent pricing, not obscuring costs, not forcing unwanted currency purchases, providing clear information before the purchase, respecting the right to withdraw, using fair and understandable terms, and protecting vulnerable consumers.

The European Commission says that games must now show the actual, real-world price of in-game items that players are able to buy using virtual currency. Additionally, games must not require players to jump through hoops with currency exchanges or use multiple currencies, which would make the actual cost of these items unclear.

On top of that, games must not make players “feel obliged to buy an excessive amount of virtual currencies to progress or enjoy the game,” and they should be allowed to withdraw from any contracts within a two-week period, including for “unused virtual currency.”

“Roughly half of Europeans play video games, making gaming a major part of our digital economy and everyday lives,” Michael McGrath, Commissioner for Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection, said in a statement .

“With that reach comes responsibility. The industry must ensure that its games do not expose players — especially children — to harmful or unfair practices. The game must be fair, and the rules must be respected. National authorities, with the support of the Commission, will make sure they are enforced.”

This is the latest big swing from the EU in the video game space after documents outlining the The EU Kids Act was shared online. This proposed legislation would require age verification for several online services, including certain multiplayer games that are “risky to minors.”

articles.title: Ordering DoorDash Is Too Hard, So an AI Agent Will Soon Be Able to Order Pizza for You
articles.summary: Ordering food through DoorDash is probably one of the biggest examples of how modern life has grown incredibly convenient, but apparently, there are still some people who think scrolling through an app is too much work. Now, you'll be able to just text DoorDash and have it order food for you without needing to figure out what, exactly, you feel like eating.
articles.body:
Ordering food through DoorDash is probably one of the biggest examples of how modern life has grown incredibly convenient, but apparently, there are still some people who think scrolling through an app is too much work. Now, you'll be able to just text DoorDash and have it order food for you without needing to figure out what, exactly, you feel like eating.

DoorDash announced the feature earlier this week, and the idea is that you'll text an AI agent through iMessages – apparently Android support will come sometime in the future – an idea of what you want for dinner. Then, DoorDash's AI agent will browse through all the restaurants in your area and give you suggestions based on your past orders and what you included in your text.

One of the examples DoorDash includes is asking its bot for your usual Friday night order, and it'll remember what you usually get, along with any modifications you usually make. This is already pretty easy to do within the app, which usually has your last few orders at the top of the screen anyways. Ironically, texting a robot for your usual order might end up having more button presses than just opening the app and ordering normally.

In some ways, this actually feels like a blast from the past. SMS ordering used to be a thing, before the rise of smartphones. Dominoes introduced a way to order pizza by sending them an emoji all the way back in 2015, according to TechTimes . Though, to be fair, that was just one restaurant.

If you want to cut scrolling through an app out of your DoorDash routine, you can sign up to test this feature on DoorDash's website , but only if you're on iOS. Android users will just have to order food the new-old-fashioned way for a while longer. It's not clear when this feature will leave beta, but either way, it seems like ordering food will get even easier, regardless of whether or not it actually needed to.

articles.title: Beware Boiúna Doesn't Deliver Enough on the Giant Snake That's the Entire Point of the Movie
articles.summary: Beware Boiúna review: You do intend to have a giant snake in your giant snake movie eventually, right?
articles.body:
Beware Boiúna is in theaters on October 2.

Movies about monstrous versions of recognizable animals are a fun subgenre. The likes of Anaconda, Lake Placid, The Meg, and the granddaddy of them all, King Kong, offer a certain innate allure regardless of their differing quality, as they take a creature we might already find menacing and mega-plus-size them. Some lean into camp, some into pure horror, and some into tragedy, but a surprising number of them work on some level.

The latest addition to this type of film is Beware Boiúna, which has its moments and a few clever twists on formulaic situations, but never quite fully takes off. On top of that, the film also suffers from just taking too damn long to get to the giant snake we’re there to see. I want to beware Boiúna, so give me Boiúna!

The film follows a trio of doctors who come to the Amazon on a humanitarian trip to administer medical assistance and, along with the crew of the boat they’re traveling on, run afoul of the legendary Boiúna — a massive fearsome snake from Brazilian mythology who is described almost like a force of nature, dispatching anyone that she sees as upsetting the balance within her home.

Though Beware Boiúna delivers a couple of early death scenes to tease the terrors to come, its set-up is far too prolonged for a film of this sort. Even at 1 hour and 44 minutes, it easily feels 15 minutes too long; Anaconda and Lake Placid knew what they were doing, running 90 minutes or less each. There are ultimately too many scenes establishing the characters and their dynamics, along with an attempt to go for a more serious-minded, grounded feeling than you might expect from a film of this sort. It’s admirable to infuse themes about the exploitation of the Amazon and its indigenous people into a giant snake movie, but it should be done far more efficiently or better blended within the mayhem people are paying to see.

The film also includes a storyline that feels like it’s part of the set-up to a totally different movie, involving a notably dark experience that med student Alli (Jessica Rothe) and ship mechanic Lena (Kiana Madeira) have that leads to “colonizer” Brennan (Logan Marshall-Green) and his men angrily tracking them from a different boat. Sure, it offers up more potential victims for Boiúna, but it’s another place where there was an easier, quicker way to get there.

When Boiúna finally unleashes, she’s pretty cool and very daunting, and the film makes good use of her unreal size as a weapon in its own right… when we can get a good look at her, that is, which isn’t enough. Director Mike P. Nelson and cinematographer Nick Junkersfeld keep Beware Boiúna often looking visually appealing, and the FX used to bring Boiúna are solid in the glimpses we get. But it quickly begins to feel like the film’s low budget is keeping her from being seen nearly as much as one would hope, including resorting to some distracting shaky-cam at points to try to disguise that fact… and this is not nearly a Jaws-level film in terms of making up for its often offscreen beast.

Veteran screenwriter Alan B. McElroy, the writer behind Halloween 4: The Return of Michael Myers — still the best Halloween sequel ever — manages to interject some deviations from the expected formula of this kind of movie. There are solid moments that play with the usual flow of who will die next, whose perspective we’re following, or what character we’re meant to like at any given moment. But at the same time, there’s not enough done in terms of delivering memorable deaths, with too many characters taken out quickly and without discernible details to make their demise stand out.

And yet there are also well-done scenes involving mosquito eggs left inside a human’s back, a snake smashing into a construction vehicle, or the particular highlight of a character needing to think fast to save themselves using the corpse of a fallen friend. But then that scene is undercut by some unnecessary flashbacks immediately afterward, providing hand-holding we simply don’t need to apparently remind the audience of a relationship we are already fully aware of. Ultimately, there’s just a lot of push-pull here.

Anchoring the film are the likable duo of Rothe and Madeira, projecting the feeling of believable resourcefulness that these characters need to have. It’s too bad Beware Boiúna doesn’t allow for Rothe to show off her impressively strong comedy chops like the Happy Death Day movies do, but better served on that front is Will Close. Close nails each of the funny lines given to his comic relief character of Callum, who’s very much out of his element even before the giant snake arrives.

Director Nelson — recently hired to direct the eleventh Saw movie — shows some flair, including the moments mentioned above or with a couple of well orchestrated jump scares, such as one that cleverly uses blurriness as a set-up. But these “that was cool” beats that are peppered throughout the film never gain enough momentum for the movie to feel like it’s truly locked in. And they can't make up for not having enough Boiúna!

articles.title: New Uncharted Game Featuring Nathan Drake Reportedly in the Works at Naughty Dog
articles.summary: A new report claims that a brand new Uncharted game featuring Nathan Drake is one of several projects in the works at Naughty Dog.
articles.body:
A new report claims that a brand new Uncharted game featuring Nathan Drake is one of several projects in the works at Naughty Dog.

MP1st has reported that the next Uncharted game, which is not a remake of any kind, is in active development at Naughty Dog. The game will feature Nathan Drake in some capacity, but it's unclear if he's the lead, in a supporting role, or even just a cameo. The project is being helmed by Shaun Escayag, who previously led Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, a standalone expansion for Uncharted 4. This has been heavily speculated for years now, with Escayag having recently teased the project himself on his socials .

The director was in Trindad earlier this year for "research" and posted a picture of a very old-looking cannon. MP1st noted that the new Uncharted game is set to be Naughty Dog's next game following the release of Intergalactic, which is speculated to launch next year. The studio recently confirmed that it will give a proper look at its upcoming sci-fi game in 2027, as well.

Uncharted Games in (Chronological) Order

Additionally, Naughty Dog confirmed it has multiple Last of Us projects in the works beyond the existing HBO TV series. Series creator Neil Druckmann has avoided revealing what mediums these projects will utilize, so they could be shows, films, books, or games. However, it feels like a safe bet that at least one of them is probably a video game, and fans are hoping it's The Last of Us Part 3.

The next Uncharted game is expected to be at least a couple of years away. Uncharted 4 was released a decade ago and put a nice bow on Nathan Drake's adventures. However, given that he remained alive and well, the door has always been left open for another escapade. Now, Drake could be joined by his daughter, Cassie, who takes a clear interest in Nathan's same hobbies.

articles.title: GTA 5 Modder Taunts Rockstar With Unofficial Nintendo Switch Port, Gets Cease and Desist from Take-Two
articles.summary: A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist.
articles.body:
A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist.

The modder, known as Mojso, was planning to bring GTA 5 and GTA Online to Nintendo Switch for modded versions of the console and got a bit cocky. After Rockstar Games recently posted its guidelines for modding (which forbids unofficial ports), the modder posted : "Try me Rockstar, [I don't give a f**k.]"

Three days later, the modder's Discord server was taken down for copyright infringement, but it didn't seem to deter them. After many warned them about how litigous Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two are, the modder suggested they aren't worried about it: "Copyright infringement is anything but enforced in Serbia."

Less than a week later, the modder confirmed they had received a cease and desist from Take-Two Interactive and thanked the company for its "mercy." As a result, the port will never see the light of day, as Mojso has stated that they don't want to risk any legal issues.

"Paralympics Productions is shutting down on October 3rd. Thank you everyone who supported us through tough times and lenghty development. I am sorry for not fulfilling your expectations and leaving you high and dry. I am thankful for Take-Two's mercy so this is the definitive end," they wrote.

When people pointed back to the modder's post about taunting Rockstar, Mojso noted that they didn't actually expect Rockstar to do anything.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

"They tried me," Mojso said . "[What the] f**k [do] you want me to do? Fight with them in court? I wasn't expecting them to hit back hard."

The modder had been working on this port using leaked GTA 5 source code, which has resulted in a bevy of other leaks and issues. Ultimately, it's probably in your best interest to not taunt massive corporations that are known for hunting down people that mess with their IP.

articles.title: Alan Ritchson Confirmed to Star in Helldivers Movie as Release Date Pushed Back
articles.summary: Reacher star Alan Ritchson has been confirmed to play one of the titular Helldivers in the game’s film adaptation, which is now set to release in 2028.
articles.body:
Reacher star Alan Ritchson has been confirmed to play one of the titular Helldivers in the hit game’s film adaptation, which is now set to release in 2028.

As told by Sony Pictures in a September 30 press release, Helldivers’ release date has been shifted from November 10, 2027 to June 9, 2028.

Justin Lin, best known for helming several of the Fast & Furious movies, is still set to direct, with Hutch Parker, PlayStation Productions’ Asad Qizilbash, and Justin Lin’s Perfect Storm Entertainment producing the film.

As described by Sony Pictures, Helldivers’ story centers on an “elite unit of soldiers — known as Helldivers — who must battle alien creatures threatening to destroy the fictional planet of Super Earth.” Ritchson will star as “one of the Helldivers,” though it remains to be seen if he is the movie’s main character or not.

Ritchson was already rumored to be involved in the Helldivers adaptation; a report from Deadline earlier this month stated the six-foot-three action hero was in talks to star. Now that this has been confirmed, we can't think of anyone better to join the Helldivers' ranks and help spread sweet, sweet Democracy through the galaxy, especially given his standout performance in Prime Video's Reacher .

The movie could have looked drastically different, and it almost did; Jason Momoa (Game of Thrones, Supergirl) was initially slated to star in Helldivers, but left the project sometime this summer for unknown reasons.

First announced in January 2025 , the Helldivers movie was received with mixed reactions from fans, especially after they learned that director Justin Lin is not a gamer. The Hollywood Reporter described this as a "strength" for Lin, saying he "leaned into it" when pitching his idea for the project.

Unsurprisingly, this caused an uproar among players... but the CEO of Arrowhead, the developer of Helldivers 2, assured them that he "trusts" Lin with the IP.

"We are not Hollywood people, and we don't know what it takes to make a movie. And therefore we don't, and shouldn't, have final say," he said, urging fans to "let him work his magic."

We're hopeful that Lin's Helldivers will be just as fantastic of a love letter to the game as Zach Cregger's Resident Evil was to Capcom's flagship horror series. It's a good time for video game adaptations overall, and more are on the horizon, with Legendary's Street Fighter set to hit theaters on October 16.

articles.title: 24 Jump Street Gets December 2027 Release Date, Original Cast Returning
articles.summary: 24 Jump Street, the long-awaited next installment in the Jonah Hill and Channing Tatum buddy cop franchise, finally has a release date.
articles.body:
24 Jump Street , the long-awaited next installment in the Jonah Hill and Channing Tatum buddy cop franchise, finally has a release date.

Sony has confirmed that 24 Jump Street will release on December 10, 2027, with Tatum, Hill, and Ice Cube all returning. The film was officially announced earlier this year after years of hopes from fans. Despite its title, it is actually the third film; there was supposed to be a third film in the 2010s which would've linked the Jump Street crew with the Men in Black, but plans for the project fell apart.

Given the extended gap between films, some thought the franchise fizzled out. However, Jonah Hill and Meghan Malloy penned a script for a new movie, which will be helmed by Rodney Rothman (Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse). It's unclear who else will star in the project or what it will be about, but given the major gap between these movies, it seems likely that the duo won't be able to integrate back into a high school or college. The first two films already made self-aware jokes about the two looking much older than the people they were supposed to be portraying undercover, so it's possible they could just continue to lean into that.

With a release next holiday season, it seems likely that shooting will begin imminently in order to hit its launch date. As a result, we may be able to expect some additional casting news any day. It's another win for those who are seeking raunchy R-rated comedies on the big screen, and hopefully, the film succeeds and can send a message to other studios that there's an appetite for other projects like it. Currently, it'll open around the same time as Avengers: Secret Wars, so it may have steep competition unless Marvel pushes that film back.

articles.title: Rockstar Suggests Disney World and SeaWorld Probably Won't Be in GTA 6
articles.summary: Rockstar has suggested that GTA 6 probably won't feature some key Florida attracts, such as Disney World and SeaWorld.
articles.body:
Rockstar has suggested that GTA 6 probably won't feature some key Florida attractions, such as Disney World and SeaWorld.

As part of a recent Game Informer cover story on GTA 6 , Rockstar Games seemed to suggest that its fictionalized version of Florida, known as Leonida, won't include every iconic staple of the sunshine state. Game Informer asked Rockstar’s senior vice president of environment art, Paul MacPherson, about some key attractions like Disney World, Seaworld, and Universal Studios, and how they would be integrated into the game. MacPherson suggested that not all of those locations will be featured in GTA 6, as they've had to be selective about what they include for the sake of narrative and game design, but maintained that the endgoal is to replicate the true Florida experience.

"We have to constantly evaluate the diversity of landscapes, towns, structures, landmarks, vistas, plant species, rock formations and everything else before we work with design and narrative to distill a list down that best works with and serves the game’s needs," he said. "So, while we may not have those exact locations, everything we have is geared to getting that full Florida experience!”

Rockstar didn't rule out any specific locations, but the comment does suggest that you won't find every major attraction in GTA 6. GTA 5 allowed players to explore the Venice Beach Boardwalk, which featured the pier and its various activities. Players could ride a rollercoaster and a ferris wheel, but generally speaking, it wasn't anything to write home about. There's no reason to do it more than once, and as a result, building an entire park around something like that may not be the best use of development resources.

The game will, however, feature a zoo for players to explore. Animals are a big part of GTA 6 , as the game will include over 170 different kinds of critters, including rare and legendary breeds which can be studied. There will be unique places to explore in-depth, even if there aren't any theme parks. Rockstar also spent an extensive amount of time in Florida, researching the area by living it directly. The studio confirmed that it even visted strip clubs and night clubs as part of its research.

articles.title: The Moza R5 Racing Wheel Offers 5.5Nm of Direct Drive Force Feedback for an Affordable Price
articles.summary: Now on sale at Best Buy.
articles.body:
If you're a big fan of racing games, you've probably already got yourself a wheel. But if you're still rocking entry level gear or a belt-driven wheel because you've been held back by the steep cost of direct drive, then check out this new deal. Best Buy is currently offering the Moza Racing R5 Direct Drive Racing Wheel and Pedal Set for PC exclusively for $349.99 with free shipping after a $30 off instant discount. That might not seem like notable savings, but keep in mind that Moza wheels are already affordable to start with and rarely see discounts throughout the entire year.

$30 Off Moza Racing R5 Direct Drive Racing Wheel for PC

Moza Racing R5 Direct Drive Racing Wheel and Pedals

The R5 is not Moza's least expensive direct drive wheel. That honor goes to the Moza R3 , which retails for $279.99 and is not currently on sale. The primary difference between the two is maximum torque: the R5 offers 5.5Nm of force compared to 3.9Nm from the R3. Both are less expensive than other alternatives: Logitech's G RS50 is $600 (for the wheel only), Fanatec's CSL DD Ready2Race Bundle is $540, Simagic's Green Flag Bundle is $600, and Thrustmaster's T598 is $466. Some do offer advantages like a higher torque ceiling or console compatibility, but if value is king, it's hard to beat Moza.

So what makes direct drive the gold standard for racing sims?

Direct drive wheels connect directly to the motor, which translates to immediate force feedback with zero latency and no lost power delivery from gear or belt-drive resistance. The higher the torque rating, the wider range of sensitivity. The Moza R5 is a big step up in immersion compared to a gear or belt driven wheel, and 5Nm is considered the baseline for bringing out the best of what direct drive has to offer.

The Moza R5 bundle includes the wheel (and wheelbase) and pedals. The 11" wheel features an aluminum alloy rim, microfiber leather grips, Moza's signature RGB sequential flow shift light indicator, and a total of 22 programmable buttons. The wheelbase features aviation-grade aluminum housing, intelligent temperature control, and a 15-bit ultra-high resolution encoder. The anti-slip pedals are constructed of high-strength steel and use Hall Effect sensors.

The Moza R5 works for PCs only, which means console gamers will need to look elsewhere. This is an excellent wheel for more competitive racing sims like Assetto Corsa, Automobilista, and Le Mans Ultimate. It will also work well with Forza Horizon 6 , although this game is more arcadey than the rest and was designed from the ground up to be controller-friendly. Assetto Corsa EVO , which is currently available as a Steam Early Access release with a final expected release in 2027, is one of the best use-case scenarios. Sadly but not surprisingly, neither Star Wars Galactic Racer nor Grand Theft Auto 6 are expected to release with wheel support (GTA itself won't see a PC port in quite a while).

articles.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Review Update
articles.summary: The best this already amazing RPG has ever been.
articles.body:
As the fantasy RPG GOAT, it really doesn’t take a whole lot for me to replay The Witcher 3. I’ve happily done so the numerous other times developer CD Projekt Red has revamped this masterpiece, but The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered seems to be the biggest overhaul to the beloved tale yet. A free update for anyone who owns the original, so many different parts of this already excellent game have been improved – from combat to movement to skill progression (not to mention the modernized graphics). After about 10 hours working my way through White Orchard and beyond, it’s already extremely clear that this is the best The Witcher 3 has ever been.

Combat is less floaty and enemies are (slightly) less stupid

It’s probably not controversial to say that one of the worst parts of this otherwise amazing adventure was the combat. Even after at least a few updates to it over the years, it still mostly felt floaty, a bit on the sloppy side, and enemies were a huge fan of just standing there and waiting for their turn to get decapitated. The modernizations made to combat in this remaster are its biggest step forward, as a whole bevy of tweaks have been made to address various sticking points. Geralt attacks faster and enemies are quicker to match your pace, which makes the process of chopping through your ninth pack of wolves much less irritating.

The camera and lock-on functionality have been the highlight so far, as you can now toggle between large groups of enemies with ease, and without the camera losing its mind. I didn’t even use the lock-on system in the original specifically because it was so unreliable, so being able to do so now has taken some serious getting used to. In general, the camera feels much better – less tightly locked to your back so you can handle groups of enemies more reliably (though those darn Neckers still like to sneak up on ya), and so far I’ve encountered far fewer situations where I felt like I was fighting my view as much as I was the monsters.

I’ve also noticed some new enemy behaviors that make swordplay more interesting, specifically how they’ll now retreat instead of letting you trounce them with steel, launch less telegraphed counterattacks, and disappear and reappear behind you (in the case of ghost monsters). All that did a much better job of making me feel like I was fighting intelligent creatures. Of course, compared to some of the stuff we see in action games today, I still do feel like the enemy behavior shows its age, and it was never all that great to begin with. Still, this is enough of an improvement to make combat feel much more engaging than it once did, significantly upgrading one of this adventure’s weakest points.

Geralt moves so much faster and Roach is less of a cretin

Movement is one of those small details that can grate the heck out of you in a massive RPG like The Witcher 3, slowly filling you with rage over the course of hundreds of hours. In the original, Geralt was often slow and had a lot of trouble getting over things. His rigid animations sometimes made me avoid ladders altogether because I just didn’t have the patience for it. In the remaster, Geralt absolutely flies over fences and navigates vertical obstacles with relative ease, to the point where it actually felt weird to see him be so nimble. I recall losing over an hour of progress in the 1.0 version when Geralt fell off a ledge no taller than a barstool and managed to break every bone in his body. This was reduced already in the next-gen update from 2022, but combined with the other speed and mobility improvements here, it almost feels like a completely different game – to the point where I’ve begun to wonder if it’ll make the map feel smaller than before as I get deeper in.

Similarly, Roach is no longer the annoying idiot she once was, now sporting much more intuitive controls that make her less likely to get caught on trees (which she now passes through if she’s just brushing against them while galloping), or end up on top of a barn. Most importantly, you can now loot herbs and whatnot without getting off your horse, which is maybe the single best improvement this remaster offers (dismounting every 10 seconds to pick a flower drove me to the brink of madness in 2015).

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered Screenshots

A pet peeve of mine in RPGs is when skill trees prevent you from playing around with different builds until you get deep into the progression. This is something The Witcher 3 suffered from quite a bit in the early hours, as so many of the impactful abilities were locked behind walls you couldn’t remove until late in the journey. The revised trees in the remaster take a page out of Cyberpunk 2077’s book by making perks more readily available earlier on, so you can customize how you’d like Geralt to get his Witchering done. I’m still early in my journey on this run, but I’m already happy to see that I won’t have to wait until I’ve invested a whole 12 points in a branch before I can unlock any good skills – so long as I’ve purchased a skill along the route I’m focusing on, I can now progress down a certain skill path with fewer obstructions.

Oh, yeah, this remaster looks pretty great too

Maybe this goes without saying for a remaster, but this is a pretty massive graphical upgrade, even over the one The Witcher 3 got for the current generation of consoles just four years ago. The lighting is much more dramatic, environmental textures are way more detailed, shadows and reflections are much more consistent across the board (especially on PC), and Geralt’s hair looks way less like a blurry mess than it once did. Again, this is all stuff that you’d hope would be the bare minimum when remastering a 12-year-old game, but it still warrants a shoutout. There’s even a new photo mode for those of you who want to take glamor shots of Geralt in all his new, high definition glory.

The one thing caveat here is that performance is still not perfect, and I still ran into a dropped frame or two on both console and PC. It’s a small price to pay for how much better things look, though, especially with the incredibly short load times I saw. And considering that the original had some framerate issues of its own, it’s not like anything has gotten worse here.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered’s greatest asset isn’t that it adds anything the original sorely lacked, but rather that it removes some of the biggest roadblocks to fun the 1.0 version was saddled with. Combat is more challenging but also easier to enjoy, movement is quicker and less irritating, and revised skill trees allow for more freedom. Even if it doesn’t manage to fix some of the technical issues (plus I’m sure there are some bugs waiting for me to encounter them that haven’t reared their ugly heads yet), it manages to make this classic RPG more enjoyable in 2026, and that’s worth yet another ride down its well-trodded roads.
